question.prompt: If \(\tan\alpha\) and \(\tan\beta\) are the roots of \(x^2-px+q=0,\) and \(\cot\alpha\) and \(\cot\beta\) are the roots of \(x^2-rx+s=0,\) then \(rs\) is necessarily

solutions.explanation:
Cotangents are reciprocals of tangents wherever both are defined, so the second quadratic has the reciprocals of the first quadratic's roots. Let
\[
u=\tan\alpha,\qquad v=\tan\beta.
\]
The assumptions ensure \(u\ne0\) and \(v\ne0\).

For a monic quadratic with roots \(u,v\), expanding its factors gives
\[
(x-u)(x-v)=x^2-(u+v)x+uv.
\]
Comparing with \(x^2-px+q\), we obtain \(u+v=p\) and \(uv=q\ne0\).

The second quadratic has roots \(1/u\) and \(1/v\). Applying the same coefficient relationships gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
r&=\frac1u+\frac1v
=\frac{u+v}{uv}=\frac pq,\\
s&=\frac1u\cdot\frac1v
=\frac1{uv}=\frac1q.
\end{aligned}
\]
These calculations remain valid for equal roots and for \(p=0\), since every denominator is nonzero. Therefore
\[
rs=\frac pq\cdot\frac1q=\frac{p}{q^2},
\]
choice C.
solutions.title: Use sums and products of reciprocal roots
